_what: Tasks, the team's to-do list, moved here from EspoCRM. tools/make-tasks.py writes this into netlify/cb/lib.mjs between the tasks:settings markers, which is the only copy the server reads. Do not hand-edit those markers; edit this and run tools/check-all.sh.
_brief: Ryan's brief, 2026-10-20: EspoCRM mostly fits, but it costs $45 a month and is not part of Stimpunks.World, which is becoming the one stop for everything; replicate its tasks iteratively. The features in use: a Kanban view, a timeline view, a list view, field filters and sorting, saved filters, Markdown and recurring tasks. Stage one is the tasks themselves and the list view with its filters and sorting; Kanban and saved filters, recurring tasks, and the timeline follow, in that order.
_numbers: Ryan's call, 2026-10-20: the street's rule against numbers beside things does not apply in tasks or in backend tools, so the list says how many tasks match and how many have each status, priority, person and tag.
_see: see: the CB_MODS roles that read and change tasks. An administrator always may. Ryan's call, 2026-10-20: directors; and since 2026-10-22 the board too (Ryan's call, after a board member could not open the office's dashboard), which the office shares, since officeAllow is tasksAllow. A task may be assigned only to somebody who can read tasks.
_board: board_hides: the statuses a board by status leaves off until somebody ticks them, so it opens on what is being worked on or could be. Canceled, chosen when the board was built on 2026-10-20; ticking it under Status puts its column back, and taking it out of this list makes it a column every time.
_repeats: repeats: how often a recurring task can come round, EspoCRM's three word for word, each as a number of days or of months. Ryan's stage three, 2026-10-20. Adding one (every 4 weeks, quarterly) is a line here and a run of tools/check-all.sh; a monthly step keeps its day of the month, or the month's last day when the month is shorter.
_colours: colours: the tag colours, in the fixed order of the dataviz method's categorical palette (its first seven slots, which pass its colour-blindness and normal-vision checks for neighbours in both light and dark), each declared in love.css as --cb-task-<colour> and --cb-task-<colour>-dark, with the ink that reads on it held in check-contrast.py. Ryan's ask, 2026-10-20: colours on tags, and on the timeline's bars. tag_colours: which colour each tag wears. Twenty-three tags cannot each have a colour anybody could tell apart, so tags take a colour by what they are about, and the legend and every tag's name say which; Weekly and Monthly say how often, not what about, and wear none. Changing a tag's colour is a line here and a run of tools/check-all.sh.
_status_colours: status_colours: the colour each status wears as a pill, after Notion's, which the team used before Tasks. Ryan's ask, 2026-10-21: Notion shows In progress in light blue, and Started keeps that light blue because Norah and Chelsea key off it, so tools/make-tasks.py refuses Started in any other colour. Not Started is Notion's gray and Completed its green, as Notion's to-do and done; Canceled is brown and Deferred yellow, Notion's colours chosen here. Each is declared in love.css as --cb-status-<colour> with --cb-status-<colour>-ink, the pale fill and the dark ink Notion uses for it, one step for light and dark themes alike so the blue is the same light blue everywhere, and each pair is held in check-contrast.py. A status always shows its name; the colour is never alone.
_lists: statuses, priorities and tags are EspoCRM's own, word for word, so the tasks brought over keep theirs. done: the statuses that mean a task needs nothing more, which the list hides until asked. Adding a tag is a line here and a run of tools/check-all.sh, as it was an administrator's edit in EspoCRM.
